subsystems.name: Sensing elements
subsystems.role: detect chemical and physical changes at extremely small scale.

subsystems.name: Power supply
subsystems.role: keep each node operating for years without maintenance.

subsystems.name: Communication
subsystems.role: relay data from billions of nodes to collection points.

subsystems.name: Deployment system
subsystems.role: distribute sensors across the atmosphere and oceans.
parts: lightweight dispensers on aircraft or balloons

subsystems.name: Data processing and AI
subsystems.role: turn raw readings into usable planetary health information.
parts: machine learning models for anomaly detection

buildSteps.title: Design the sensor node
buildSteps.detail: Combine a sensing element, a tiny radio, a power harvester and a processor on a single chip using semiconductor fabrication methods.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate at scale
buildSteps.detail: Use wafer-scale manufacturing to produce millions of identical nodes cheaply, with testing built into the line.

buildSteps.title: Package for harsh environments
buildSteps.detail: Seal each node against salt water, pressure, temperature swings and biofouling while leaving the sensor exposed.

buildSteps.title: Integrate power and communication
buildSteps.detail: Attach energy harvesters and antennas, then program the node to sleep, wake, sense and transmit in a low-duty cycle.

buildSteps.title: Deploy by natural forces
buildSteps.detail: Release nodes from aircraft, ships or balloons so that winds and ocean currents spread them across target regions.

buildSteps.title: Form a self-organising network
buildSteps.detail: Nodes discover neighbours, build mesh routes and forward data hop-by-hop to gateways or satellites.

buildSteps.title: Collect and analyse data
buildSteps.detail: Aggregate streams in the cloud, run AI models to detect changes, and feed results to environmental monitoring systems.

buildSteps.title: Maintain and recycle
buildSteps.detail: Design nodes to degrade safely or be recovered, and replace failed units with new deployments as needed.

prerequisites.why: many chemical and physical sensors exist at micro-scale, but not yet with the sensitivity, lifetime and cost needed for billions of units.
solar and vibration harvesters work in labs, but powering a node for years in dark or deep-ocean conditions remains difficult.
protocols for sensor networks are proven at thousands of nodes, but scaling to billions with intermittent connectivity is unsolved.

prerequisites.tech: Autonomous deployment by atmospheric and ocean currents
prerequisites.why: no method yet exists to release and track vast numbers of tiny sensors reliably across the planet.

prerequisites.tech: AI for massive, noisy data streams
prerequisites.why: machine learning can process large datasets, but handling billions of continuous, heterogeneous environmental readings is beyond current practice.

pathway.milestone: Earth observation satellites, ocean profiling floats (e.g. Argo) and regional IoT sensor networks
pathway.unlocks: large-scale but sparse monitoring of climate, oceans and air quality.

pathway.milestone: Dense regional sensor networks using low-power wide-area radio and energy harvesting
pathway.unlocks: city- and basin-scale real-time tracking of pollutants and weather.

pathway.milestone: Self-powered micro-sensors deployed by drones or balloons in pilot studies
pathway.unlocks: proof that tiny nodes can survive and communicate in the wild.

pathway.milestone: Global sensory web with autonomous deployment, mesh networking and AI analysis
pathway.unlocks: continuous, planet-wide monitoring of chemical and physical changes.
